order: Update the release changelog to record what the first hour of cross-platform continuous integration actually found. Name the four runner faults that surfaced and were fixed in this release — the shell-launch fault, the path-comparison guarantee that failed to hold under symlinks and short file names, the refusal path that wrote before it objected, and the sweep step that under-reported its own scope. Note the one negative-control check that reports itself inconclusive under one platform's shell, so a future reader does not mistake it for a passing proof. Add a field-validation line documenting the shim case that continuous integration can prove but cannot stage against a real user's PATH. Bring the changelog's stated check count into sync with the suite's actual total, moving it from ninety-four to exactly ninety-six. Keep the change confined to documentation only — the changelog, the readme, and the field-validation notes — with no source or test-code edits of any kind.
claims: We recorded the four cross-platform runner faults that the first hour of continuous integration surfaced and this release fixed, noted the one negative control that reports inconclusive under one platform's shell, and added a field-validation line for the shim case that integration testing can prove but not stage on a real PATH. The change was documentation only, touching exactly three files with 54 insertions and 10 deletions. Check counts were synced from 94 to exactly 96 to match the suite's current total.
